title: Kollar's lemma: a Noetherian local ring is Artinian, regular of dimension one, of depth at least two, or has a finite birational-type extension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring. Consider the four properties: (1) $R$ is Artinian (every descending chain of ideals of $R$ is stationary); (2) $R$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; (3) $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge2$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]; (4) there is a ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$ to a nonzero commutative ring $R'$ such that $R'$ is finitely generated as an $R$-module through $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is not an isomorphism, there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak m^n\cdot\ker(\varphi)=0$ and $\mathfrak m^n R'\subseteq\varphi(R)$, and $\mathfrak m$ is not an associated prime of the $R$-module $R'$, i.e. there is no $z\in R'$ whose annihilator $\{a\in R:\varphi(a)z=0\}$ equals $\mathfrak m$. Then (i) at least one of (1)-(4) holds, and (ii) (3) and (4) do not hold together.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BHZ (lemma-hart-serre-loc-thm, line 28923; due to Kollar), with its proof: (i) is 'every R falls into one of the 4 cases', (ii) is the final paragraph '(3) excludes (4)'
